MOTION FOE INTERVENTION 
Comes now Hazard Perry County Community Ministries, by and through counsel, 
and for its Notion for Intervention in the above matter states as follows: 
Hazard Perry County Community Ministries objects to the proposal for several 
reasons. It’s interests differ from those of the Pike County Senior Citizens Program in that it 
serves a wider array of individuals and runs a number of different programs that would be 
placed in jeopardy with the rate increase. Since 1976, Community Ministries has served 
families and individuals in need. It currently operates a homeless shelter, rental housing for 
homeless families, homelessness prevention assistance, and two childcare centers. Hazard 
Perry County Community Ministries is the last bastion of shelter for many in the community 
and keeps many others from being homeless. It also allows many individuals the chance to 
work or continue their education by providing affordable and reliable child care. The scope 
of its coverage is far broader than that of the Pike County Senior Citizens Program and it has 
interests that will not be addressed by their intervention. Thus, Hazard Perry County 
Community Ministries should be allowed to intervene and voice its objection to the 
Page 1 of 6

proposed rate increase. 
Hazard Perry County Community Ministries objects to this proposed rate increase 
because little to nothing is known about its justification. Kentucky Power has not explained 
how this will improve its service, or why they cannot make ends meet with the current rates 
in place. Because Kentucky Power basically has a monopoly on their industry in this region, 
it is imperative that they be required to make its customers aware of the reasoning behind 
this rate increase of astronomical proportions. Without proper checks and balances such as 
requiring Kentucky Power to provide the basis for the requested increase and allowing 
affected entities to address them, the potential for abuse is great. 
Hazard Perry County Community Ministries serves mostly low income individuals 
Most of the people who live in its rental housing are fbrthering their education and/or 
working low wage jobs. These individuals can barely afford to pay their electricity hills now. 
With a proposed rate increase of 33.430/0, they will be face with an untenable 
choice-whether they can keep the lights on or keep their children fed. 
In addition, Hazard Perry County Community Ministries has a unique perspective 
on the utility market in Perry County. As part of the services provided, families come to 
Hazard Perry County Community Ministries with electric bills in arrears or shutoff notices. 
Hazard Perry County Community Ministries then can step in with its homelessness 
prevention assistance. In 2009, Hazard Perry County Community Ministries served 
approximately 100 individuals with $5,000 toward Kentucky Power bill assistance. With 
the proposed rate increase, it is estimated that the number of people requesting assistance 
will double. However, Hazard Perry County Community Minisitriest will not have the 
funds to intervene on behalf of all of those seeking assistance. Both the families who are 
Page 2 of 6

unable to pay their bill will lose, and so will Kentucky Power, as they spend even more 
money on labor to conduct shutoffs and lose customers. 
Finally, as a 50l(c)(3) nonprofit organization and small business the rate increase 
would have dire effects. The funding of hazard Perry County Community Ministries is 
limited to that which can be obtain through grants, donations, and fees for service. In the 
recently composed 2010 budget, Hazard Perry County Community Ministries was barely 
able to make it break even. The proposed rate increase would literally break the budget and 
leave the agency, like its clients, an impossible choice-whether to keep the lights on or pay 
the staff. Hazard Perry County Community Ministries can only be effective if it can do 
both. An increase of one third in the utilities costs would require programs or positions to be 
cut in order to meet operating expenses with the limited available funds of the agency. It 
would truly be a sad day if homeless individuals were turned away from the shelter because 
it could no longer operate or if motivated individuals had to quit school or their jobs because 
child care was no longer available. 
Rased upon the foregoing reasons, Hazard Perry County Community Ministries 
should be allowed to intervene to protect its interests that are distinct from those of the Pike 
County Senior Citizens Program. 
Respectfully submitted,
